newsitem.title: HUNGARY: COURT RULES HUNGARY'S FIRST TOLL ROAD TOO DEAR.
newsitem.headline: COURT RULES HUNGARY'S FIRST TOLL ROAD TOO DEAR.

text.p: A Budapest district court has ruled that the fees charged on Hungary's first toll road, part of the Budapest-Vienna motorway, are excessively high, Hungarian news agency MTI reported on Tuesday.
The court ruling was sought by the Hungarian motoring organisation Magyar Autoklub.

The court decided that a reasonable toll for cars using the 43-kilometre section on the Hungarian side of the Austrian border would be 550 forints as against the 1,000 forints currently charged by the motorway concession company ELMKA. The ruling was based on comparison with other countries.

ELMKA's managing director Karoly Lederer said his company set its tolls in line with a concession contract it signed with the Hungarian government in 1993 which stipulated a toll of 350 forints at 1992 prices.
Lederer said ELMKA would appeal and warned that the government would "face the consequences" if the appeal failed.
